newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: GOOD ECONOMIC NEWS EXPECTED
Australia's trade position is tipped to look a little brighter this morning, with the December balance of payments figures due out.
A figure of around 1.6 billion dollars is expected, much better than November's 1.92 billion, a blowout of six percent.
Although imports rose in December, Macquarie Bank Chief Economist, Bill Shields, says exports should also have risen.

But Mr Shields says today's expected good news won't have a bearing on interest rates, with inflation figures and the Government's budget review, both revealed earlier this week, He says the current account has been fairly steady in the past year, at about four per cent of GDP, meaning it's had little impact on interest rate decisions.
The Bureau of Statistics will also announce today, whether it'll go ahead with plans to scrap the monthly release of balance of payments figures, in favour of a quarterly report.
WOOLDRIDGE SET TOUGH TASK IN CHARM STAKES
Federal Health Minister, Michael Wooldridge, returns to Canberra today to face a storm over proposals to ban non-immunised children from schools.
Federal Schools Minister, David Kemp, will ask State Education Ministers to consider the proposal at a summit next month, but already the states have expressed opposition to the plan.
Dr Wooldridge has supported Dr Kemp's call, but appears to have his work cut out for him in talking the states around.
Dr Wooldridge has been on a tour of Northern Territory Aboriginal towns.
States and Territories have criticised Dr Kemp's plan, saying it is too harsh and impractical.
FLOODS CAUSING TROUBLE IN THREE STATES
Floods continue to cause major problems in New South Wales, Queensland and the far north of Western Australia.
In the latest flooding there's been major damage to homes, schools, hotels and roads in the popular coastal Kimberley town of Broome, in Western Australia.
More rain is forecast for the Kimberley, with further flooding expected on the Fitzroy River and its tributaries.
In New South Wales, State Emergency Services have prepared thousands of sandbags to guard against more flooding at Narrabri in the north of the state.
SES duty officer, Neville Clark, says 10-thousand sandbags have been readied in the Narrabri area.
And in north western Queensland, floodwaters from torrential rain have closed a number of roads to conventional traffic.
They include the Kennedy and Diamantina Developmental Roads and the Capricorn and Landsborough Highways in the Longreach district.
Some roads are also closed in inland New South Wales.
At last report the Gwydir and Newell Highways near Moree were open, although water is flowing over them.
COMMONWEALTH GIVES LAND RIGHTS ACT THUMBS UP
The Federal Government says the mining provisions of the Northern Territory Land Rights Act are working reasonably well.
One of the recommendations of the Wran Committee on Darwin report released 18 months ago, was that the act be reviewed, because the mining provisions, including the veto, were delaying development.
The Federal Government's official response to the Wran report has been released this week.
It addresses the report's 77 recommendations, but says the mining provisions of the act have been working reasonably well in recent times.
VIC, SA, "NOT COMMITTED TO COMPETITION POLICY"
Queensland Treasurer, Joan Sheldon, has accused Victoria and South Australia of hypocrisy over their complaints about proposals to cut car industry tariffs.
Mrs Sheldon is angry that Queensland is expected to buy cheap electricity from Victoria, and to lower sugar tariffs, but Victoria and South Australia aren't prepared to do the same.
She says those states only seem committed to the national competition policy when it suits them.
Mrs Sheldon says she'll continue to lobby the Federal Government to ensure all states are treated fairly under the reforms.
REDFERN DEMOLITIONS A STEP CLOSER
A key recommendation of last week's Redfern summit has been achieved in part.
South Sydney Council has fast-tracked the approval of a demolition application for three derelict houses in Eveleigh street, but has refused one because it is still occupied.
The Aboriginal Housing Company, which owns the terraces, already has permission to pull down another eight houses in Eveleigh Street, but hasn't yet done so.
However, a group opposed to redevelopment plans, the Redfern Aboriginal Housing Coalition, says it will be seeking an injunction against the demolition work.
AUSSIE SPRINTER'S HEARING POSTPONED
Australian sprinter Dean Capobianco's drugs ban case with the International Amateur Athletic Federation has been postponed until the middle of March.
The Federation says the delay was requested by the athlete, so the hearing would not clash with his grand prix commitments.
Capobianco tested positive for the anabolic steroid stanozolol at a meeting in The Netherlands in May last year.
Charges against him were dropped just before the Atlanta Olympics last July, enabling him to compete, after Athletics Australia ruled that the test procedure was flawed.
The IAAF is appealing against that decision.
Capobianco, who has strongly denied taking performance enhancing drugs, faces a four-year ban if he loses the case.
MAKING NEWS IN SPORT
CRICKET
Two day-night Sheffield Shield matches enter their second day's play this afternoon.

In the top of the table clash in Brisbane, a close tussle is developing for first innings points between Queensland, dismissed for 179, and Western Australia, which is four for 102. The first day was dominated by bowlers but the Warriors appear to have the advantage.
And at the MCG, Victoria will resume at one for 12 today, chasing the New South Wales total of 290.
The Australian Cricket Board says it will not allow a Sheffield Shield match to be moved from Perth's WACA ground for the Australian Baseball League finals.
The WACA-based Perth Heat is currently at the top of the league, and looks set to play in a home play-off series starting on February 14.
However, the games clash with a Shield match between Western Australia and Queensland.
GOLF
A course record-equalling 65 by New Zealander Greg Turner has given him a one-stroke lead after the first round of the Vines Classic in Perth.
Turner leads fellow Kiwi Frank Nobilo who carded a six-under 66.
Australia's Wayne Grady and Englishman Miles Tunnicliff share third place at five-under.
